deposits.notes:
Paper-specific deposit identified in PDF p. 9 and independently present in forms/c249.json:data_and_code.code_url; the form has no data URL. Repository webpage HTTP 200. GitHub recursive-tree API HTTP 200, truncated=false, commit 74b79b65f221a01ba9c6744dc4f107741fcd8908; 37 files, all listed below. API URL: https://api.github.com/repos/tsinghua-fib-lab/human-ai-consensus/git/trees/HEAD?recursive=1 . Files were read from immutable URLs under https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tsinghua-fib-lab/human-ai-consensus/74b79b65f221a01ba9c6744dc4f107741fcd8908/ . Thirty-six files were fetched without authentication, each HTTP 200 and matching its API-listed byte size. The third-party concreteness workbook was inventoried but not downloaded. No downloaded files or executed repository scripts were written to disk.

Primary inspected table: processed_data/panel_adj.pkl, 8640 player-round rows, the 10 columns in columns_checked, with no missing cells and no duplicate (run_key, uid, round) keys. Conditions are explicitly encoded by agent_ratio, agent_style and agent_basem. Participant identity is uid within run_key; uid_fe combines them. Human IDs start human_ and agent IDs start agent_ in the eight human-containing conditions. The extra 100%-agent run has numeric-string IDs and must be excluded from human counts. Rounds are indexed 0-39. Each of nine condition/run combinations has 24 players and 960 rows. The eight human-containing conditions contain 127 condition-specific human IDs: S1 baseline 24; 12.5% 21; 33.3% neutral/32B 16; 50% 12; 75% 6; S2 high-adoption 16 and high-persistence 16; S3 neutral/7B 16. These are observed deposited analysis records, not a recruitment or exclusion audit.

All eight randomized human conditions are covered by participant-level y and y_adj consensus scores. analyze_convergence_new.py (final_adjusted_values) and plot_fig3_combined_continuous.py (lines 243-254 at the inspected commit) explicitly use each player’s final-round y_adj for the consensus boxplots. The same Agents 33%|Neutral|32B run is selected for both trait and capability comparisons. The scores for human players still measure similarity to the mixed human/agent group; merely filtering panel rows to humans does not turn y or y_adj into human-only pairwise diversity.

processed_data/intermediate_result/final_expressions_all.csv: 720 rows; columns condition, agent_ratio, round, player_id, player_type, expression. processed_data/intermediate_result/perspective_annotations_v3.csv: 720 rows; the same six columns plus is_last, analogical, holistic, event. Both tables were fully read; no missing cells and no duplicate (condition, round, player_id) keys. They cover rounds 36-40 using 1-based round labels for five neutral/32B S1 conditions (0%, 12.5%, 33.3%, 50%, 75%) and an additional all-agent condition. The five S1 arms contain 395 human-output rows from 79 condition-specific humans, with 5 texts per human. Human-only final-round or final-five-round diversity can therefore be recomputed including the pure-human baseline. Annotation values can be aggregated within person before calculating arm summaries. These CSVs do not contain the S2 trait or S3 7B conditions.

Full mixed-arm interaction histories were read from processed_data/A4.pkl (12.5% agents, 21 humans), A3.pkl (33.3%, 16 humans), A2.pkl (50%, 12 humans), and A5.pkl (75%, 6 humans). Filename-to-condition mapping is explicit in plot_ai_penalty_with_controls_with_centrality_distance.py line 42 and analyze_human_agent_separately.py lines 578-581. Each file contains one run (key 0), 24 player histories of length 40, and 480 paired-interaction records in tracker fields players, answers, outcome. simulation is keyed by player ID and has my_history, peer_history, interactions, outcome, score_history. All 120 final-five-round CSV texts in each of these four arms exactly match the corresponding history text for the same player and round. Full-round raw descriptions were not found for the 0% baseline, S2 manipulations or S3 7B arm; the baseline’s final-five-round texts are nevertheless present.

The adoption_series_dict_with_individual_results.pkl and persistence_series_dict_with_individual_results.pkl files were read from processed_data/intermediate_result/. Each contains six condition dictionaries: four mixed S1 arms plus the two S2 trait arms. per_individual stores ids, roles, rounds, adoption or persistence, and counts; each score matrix is 24 by 39. Missing transition scores occur in several arms and must be handled using the stored matrices/counts. The released plotting code pools per-person window means, then uses sample SD/sqrt(n) for its SEM; its first/last 20 columns overlap by one column in a 39-column matrix. This permits auditing the phase definitions but does not settle every discrepancy with the paper’s round indexing or printed tests. No 0% baseline or 7B condition is included in these two caches.

Other inspected files: consensus_dict_remove_ind.pkl has raw and adjusted condition/round aggregates for all nine conditions (40 rows per condition in each dictionary), with mean_consensus, std_consensus, sem_consensus and, in the adjusted data, N_participants. These aggregate columns are not substitutes for human-specific statistics. all_contribution_results_v2w.pkl contains group-level lexical/conceptual contribution and CLR summaries, without participant-level contribution estimates. attractor_dynamics_dict.pkl includes player IDs, round maps, texts and embeddings for the four mixed S1 conditions.

The eight questionnaire CSVs were also read. Common-question files A2/A3/A4/A5 contain respectively 12/16/21/6 rows, columns agreement and ai_leadership; personalized-question files contain respectively 108/144/189/54 rows, columns round, you, peer, judged_ai, willingness. They lack an explicit participant-ID column, so repeated questionnaire rows cannot be assumed to be directly linkable to unique people. The condition mapping is supplied by the code and filenames.

Coverage limits: one deposited run per condition; no independent session replication or recruitment/exclusion-flow file. Locally reused human_ IDs do not establish cross-session real-world identity. There is one shared neutral comparator in the released analyses, but identifiers cannot independently establish whether a person attended more than one differently coded session. S2/S3 scores are available, while human-only text diversity for their manipulated arms is not confirmed. Repository root LICENSE is MIT (copyright 2026 FIB LAB, Tsinghua University); no separate study-data-specific license was identified.

what_we_could_compute: final.open_items[1]: Count the humans represented in the consensus analysis by condition and their available rounds; all eight human conditions have complete 40-round panel records. Determine outcome-specific nonmissing counts for posted annotations and adoption/persistence matrices. Recruitment exclusions and reasons for missing transition scores remain unavailable.

final.open_items[3], S1-O1/S2-O1/S3-O1: Compute each human’s final-round and across-round consensus summaries, arm means, sample SDs and conventional participant-based SEs from y/y_adj. The plotting code identifies player-level boxplot observations and the files identify a single run per condition. These SEs do not establish valid uncertainty across independently replicated sessions, and stored consensus scores use mixed human-agent comparison pools.

final.open_items[5]: Identify the single posted neutral 33.3%/32B comparison dataset selected in the S1, S2 and S3 analysis scripts, so its records can be reused without counting the comparator as three independent samples. The released condition-local pseudonyms do not independently verify real-world cross-session participant overlap.

final.open_items[6]: Recompute human-only between-person text/idea diversity for all five S1 arms using final-round texts or person-level aggregation of rounds 36-40, with condition and human/agent labels. Compute per-person annotation means and arm means, SDs and conventional SEs for analogical, holistic and event scores. Full-round trajectories can be recomputed in the four mixed S1 arms. This addresses availability of a qualifying human-only comparison; the direction and magnitude still require a separate analysis.

final.open_items[8]: Compute per-human early/late adoption and persistence summaries, arm means, SDs, conventional SEs and analyzed counts for the four mixed S1 arms and both S2 trait arms. Audit pooling and phase-window choices in the posted code. Full S1 histories permit alternative round-aligned calculations and reconstruction of movement/influence measures; paper/code indexing and test discrepancies require further reconciliation.

Not resolved by the deposit: student/occupational status (open_items[2]), physical versus remote setting (open_items[7]), full recruitment/exclusion flow, independently replicated session uncertainty, or human-only text diversity for the manipulated S2/S3 arms. The questionnaire files lack explicit participant IDs, limiting person-level summaries of self-reported willingness and the peer-centroid gap in open_items[4].
notes: Checked the entire markdown conversion (542 lines, 86885 characters) and the 29-page source PDF, including Supplementary Information on pp. 16-29. Quotes are exact spans of PDF text extraction, preserving original line breaks and Unicode; superscript reference 34 is flattened by extraction. No preregistration, embargo or on-request data statement was found. The main availability statement alone understates the public repository: participant/output records, assignments and scores were directly inspected, supporting public_participant_data despite incomplete coverage of some outcomes and raw texts. Only the named output JSON was written; all remote data stayed in memory, and no repository code was executed. The preprint landing page https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.02122 and its paper-linked version https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.02122v1 both returned HTTP 200. The landing page lists only v1 (2 September 2026), matching the local version; no journal reference or separate supplementary-data file was identified there. The supplement is embedded in the PDF. The bibliographic spaCy DOI https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.1212303 also returned HTTP 200 and redirected to https://zenodo.org/records/10009823. Its named API endpoint https://zenodo.org/api/records/1212303 returned HTTP 200 and the record explosion/spaCy: v3.7.2: Fixes for APIs and requirements. It lists one file, explosion/spaCy-v3.7.2.zip, 20272814 bytes, and license cc-by-4.0. This is third-party NLP software, not a c249 deposit, and is excluded from deposits; its archive was not downloaded. All four required deposit-search services were queried by title and first-author name; DataCite and Zenodo also received focused author-plus-consensus searches. Broad author-name queries were not exhaustively paginated, as documented in searches. Zenodo initially rejected size=100 with HTTP 400; the public size=25 requests succeeded. No new c249 data deposit was identified. The final confidence is high for the affirmative availability finding because the actual public data columns and values were inspected, rather than inferred from filenames or the paper’s claim.
